title: Ancient DNA Extraction from Dental Calculus with Consolidant Removal
author: Franziska Aron
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bqbmmsk6
materials: Prepare cleaned workspace with all necessary reagents and equipment. If lab-wide large-batch pre-prepared reagent stores are used, ensure to have made personal stock-aliquot of reagents such as UV-Water, EDTA, sodium acetate, and proteinase K in amounts sufficient for this extraction.
Irradiate all buffers with UV for 00:30:00 without the lids. UV irradiation can be done together with solutions from steps 1 (binding buffer), 4 (wash buffer), and 5 (TET buffer).
Prepare cleaned workspace with all necessary reagents and equipment.

steps.title: Prepare binding buffer
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amount of guanidine hydrochloride (GuHCl) into a glass bottle, clean the work area first with water then bleach (never add bleach directly to GuHCl). Add 6 mL UV‑irradiated HPLC water, shake horizontally until the salt dissolves (use short 10 s bursts at ~400 W in a microwave with the tube slightly unscrewed if needed, allowing cooling between bursts). Add 4 mL isopropanol to bring the total volume to 10 mL per reaction. Store the buffer at 4 °C overnight (day 4), label with name, date and number of reactions, seal with parafilm and keep refrigerated for up to four weeks.

steps.title: Prepare wash buffer aliquot
steps.instruction: Pipette 40 mL ethanol from the High Pure Viral Nucleic Acid kit into a container, then aliquot 900 µL per reaction for later use.

steps.title: Prepare TET elution buffer
steps.instruction: Make an aliquot of 100 µL TE‑buffer per reaction and add Tween‑20 to reach a final concentration of 0.05 % (v/v). Because Tween‑20 is viscous, first dilute it 1:10 in UV‑HPLC water (10 % solution) and add the appropriate volume of this dilution to the TE‑buffer.

steps.title: Dilute proteinase K
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg proteinase K powder in 10 mL UV‑HPLC water to obtain a 10 mg · mL⁻¹ working solution. Store the solution at –20 °C for use on day 2.

steps.title: UV‑sterilize calculus
steps.instruction: Place 2–5 mg of calculus in the appropriate container (powder in original tube with lid open; large pieces in an aluminium foil boat). Irradiate for 1 min, shake, then irradiate for another 1 min. If the sample has been pre‑treated with acetone, irradiate for only 30 s. Use a UV cross‑linker; for large pieces keep the boat in the cross‑linker to maximise exposure.

steps.title: EDTA surface wash
steps.instruction: If the calculus was in a foil boat, transfer it back to a 1.5 mL or 2 mL tube. Add 1 mL of 0.5 M EDTA to each sample to remove surface contaminants (skip this step only when the study aims to detect infectious pathogens).

steps.title: Vortex and short incubation
steps.instruction: Vortex the tube and incubate on a rotator at room temperature for 15 min. For very powdery samples the supernatant may be removed directly after vortexing, omitting the incubation.

steps.title: Centrifuge and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Spin the tubes for 2 min at 18 500 × g (temperature not specified). Transfer the supernatant to a new tube labelled “EDTA‑wash” and store at –20 °C for possible future analyses. Add a fresh 1 mL of 0.5 M EDTA to each remaining pellet.

steps.title: Overnight EDTA incubation
steps.instruction: Seal the tubes with parafilm, place on a low‑speed rotator (12–16 rpm) at room temperature and rotate overnight (12–18 h). If the tubes will be exposed to UV, cover them with foil. After incubation the suspension can be stored at –20 °C.

steps.title: Remove parafilm and check tubes
steps.instruction: Take off the parafilm, inspect for leaks (clean any leaks), and briefly centrifuge to remove liquid from the lids.

steps.title: Add proteinase K and decalcify
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of 10 mg · mL⁻¹ proteinase K to each tube, vortex, reseal with parafilm and rotate at 12–16 rpm, room temperature for 24–48 h (monitor until the calculus is fully decalcified, appearing buoyant, feathery or disappearing). Store the suspension at –20 °C after decalcification.

steps.title: Prepare extraction set‑up
steps.instruction: For each reaction gather: one 50 mL Falcon tube, one High Pure Extender Assembly (Falcon tube with funnel and purification column), two collection tubes from the kit, and one 1.5 mL LoBind tube for the final elution.

steps.title: Add sodium acetate to binding mix
steps.instruction: In each 50 mL Falcon tube pipette 10 mL binding buffer and 400 µL UV‑irradiated sodium acetate. Mix by inversion and measure pH (target 5–6). If pH is high, add more sodium acetate; if low, add sodium hydroxide.

steps.title: Pellet calculus after decalcification
steps.instruction: Remove parafilm from the decalcification tubes, spin for 2 min at 18 500 × g (temperature not specified) to pellet the calculus. If the pellet is not solid, repeat the centrifugation.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to binding tube
steps.instruction: Pipette the supernatant into the corresponding 50 mL Falcon tube, mix by inversion, and store the calculus pellet at –20 °C.

steps.title: Bind DNA to column
steps.instruction: Pipette the binding‑buffer / extract mixture into the High Pure Extender Assembly (funnel).

steps.title: Centrifuge binding step
steps.instruction: Spin the assembly at the maximum speed of the 50 mL Thermo Scientific TX‑400 swinging‑bucket rotor (≈1500 rpm, convert to the appropriate rcf) for 8 min. After 4 min, turn the tube 180° to prevent liquid from sticking to the funnel rim.

steps.title: Collect flow‑through
steps.instruction: Pipette any remaining liquid from the funnel onto the column, remove the funnel and place the column into a fresh 2 mL collection tube. Discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Dry spin column (first)
steps.instruction: Dry spin the column in its collection tube for 2 min at 18 500 × g.

steps.title: First wash of column
steps.instruction: Add 450 µL wash buffer (from the High Pure Viral Nucleic Acid kit) to the column and spin at 8000 × g for 1 min.

steps.title: Second wash of column
steps.instruction: Remove the column, discard the used collection tube, place the column into a fresh 2 mL collection tube and repeat the 450 µL wash and 1 min spin at 8000 × g. Discard the flow‑through either by pipetting it out or by pouring it into a waste tube, then pat the tube rim dry with a single spot of paper tissue and clean the work surface with DNA‑Away or bleach.

steps.title: Final dry spin
steps.instruction: Dry spin the column at 18 500 × g for 1 min. Optionally spin for 30 s, turn the tube 180°, then spin another 30 s.

steps.title: First DNA elution
steps.instruction: Transfer the column to a fresh 1.5 mL LoBind tube, add 50 µL TET buffer to the centre of the column, incubate on the benchtop for 3 min, then spin for 1 min at 18 500 × g to elute DNA. Label the tube on top and side.

steps.title: Second DNA elution
steps.instruction: Repeat the elution step with another 50 µL TET buffer to obtain a total elution volume of 100 µL.

steps.title: Store DNA extracts
steps.instruction: Store the eluted DNA extracts at –20 °C.

steps.title: Optional acetone wash
steps.instruction: If consolidants are present, add 500 µL acetone to each sample, soak with the lid open under a fume hood for 15 min, centrifuge at 15 800 rcf, 22 °C for 1 min, remove acetone with a pipette and discard. Leave the tube open to allow residual acetone to evaporate until the calculus is dry.
